sections.h2: Which offices send an Alpharetta property tax bill?
sections.html:
Alpharetta owners deal with two billing offices. The Fulton County Tax Commissioner collects for Fulton County government, the schools and the State of Georgia. The City of Alpharetta handles its own city tax: its website lists Property Tax Accounts among its payment options and Homestead Exemptions among its applications. The Tax Commissioner's list of cities it collects for names Atlanta, Mountain Park, Sandy Springs, Johns Creek and Chattahoochee Hills, not Alpharetta.

The Fulton County Board of Tax Assessors sets the value on which both bills rely. A city that bills on its own collects through its clerk or finance office, with the county handling county and school levies. Pull both bills for your parcel so each payment reaches the right office.

A Tax Commissioner customer service center sits at 11575 Maxwell Road, Alpharetta, GA 30022, with weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county tax line is 404-613-6100.

Expect the 2026 Fulton County bill to differ from a normal one. The digest ran late because the assessors had an unprecedented number of land packages to process. A Fulton County Superior Court order then allowed temporary bills built from 2025 millage rates and the partial digest.

Final millage rates come from each taxing body after the digest is complete, and the county said a refund or a corrected final bill follows where needed. An owner who paid an estimate should watch for a corrected bill and keep the receipt.

Alpharetta's own due date is whatever the city bill prints, and the city Finance Department can confirm it.

Matching a question to the right office
QuestionOffice to ask
Disputing a valueFulton County Board of Tax Assessors
Paying the county and school billFulton County Tax Commissioner
Paying the city bill, filing a city homestead exemptionCity of Alpharetta Finance Department
Recording a deed, proving transfer tax paidClerk of Superior Court

A dispute is a written filing with the assessors, due 45 days after the notice was mailed, and it names a Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator hearing. Payments go to the county tax office, never to the assessors.

The state homestead exemption knocks $2,000 off the assessed value, which itself is 40 percent of market value. You can apply any time once the home is your primary residence, up to April 1 of the first year you want the exemption, and an owner who never applies forfeits it.

Returns are due from January 1 to April 1, and a taxpayer who skips one is treated as repeating last year's return. Alpharetta takes its own homestead filing, so confirm that both the city and the county list your exemption.

  • Find the exemption line on the county bill.
  • Find the exemption line on the city bill.
  • Give both offices the right mailing address after a sale.

sections.h2: Does an Alpharetta mailing address mean the house is inside the city?
sections.html:
Not always, and the answer decides which offices bill you. The Halcyon mixed-use development carries an Alpharetta postal address but lies in Forsyth County, outside the city limits and outside Fulton County. Alpharetta's northeast edge touches unincorporated Forsyth County, and its other borders are Milton, Roswell and Johns Creek, each with its own city government.

Look at the parcel number and the tax bill instead of the mailing address when you confirm the taxing jurisdictions that apply to a house.

Know which taxing bodies apply before you set a price. Alpharetta sits in northern Fulton County, about 26 miles north of downtown Atlanta. The 2020 census counted 65,818 residents in 24,727 households, with 26,089 housing units. Because buyers searching by city name may land on homes in neighboring jurisdictions, confirm the jurisdiction early when you price and advertise.

Steps for a seller: first, look up the parcel on the Tax Commissioner's site and write down the parcel ID. Second, check whether the city also holds a bill. Third, confirm your homestead exemption appears on both. Fourth, ask each office for a balance before you sign a listing agreement, and save the written answers in your closing folder so the title company can see exactly what was owed on each date. Doing this first avoids a surprise payoff late in the contract period and gives buyers a clear picture of what the annual bill looks like for that address.

The owner on January 1 carries the year's tax, with no partial-year refund. Transfer tax comes due before the deed is recorded, the seller is the liable party unless the contract says otherwise, and the PT-61 form is filed online with the state's clerks' cooperative.

County tax liens are recorded on the general execution docket at the clerk's office. Before listing, request a balance statement from the Tax Commissioner and from the city, and ask whether any 2026 estimated payment remains open. Give the title company both statements so the payoff is ready on closing day, and ask the closing attorney to confirm that the county and city shares are each shown on the settlement statement. A cash sale skips lender escrow steps, yet it still needs both balances confirmed.

sections.h2: How to find and pay the county half of the bill
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's office combines the assessors' value and exemption data with millage rates from the county commission and other governing bodies, then mails bills to the address the assessors hold. After a sale or inheritance, that matters: if the assessors have an old address, the bill goes there.

The commissioner's website has two lookups, and the same site accepts card or e-check payment:

  • Search a bill by whole or partial parcel ID, account number or street address.
  • Ask for a combined summary of several parcels when you hold their full parcel IDs.

For walk-in help, Maxwell Road is nearest. The county also lists a downtown Atlanta office at 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, and a North Fulton Service Center at 7741 Roswell Road NE in Sandy Springs, each on the 404-613-6100 line.

You can ask for a refund in writing. A claim over tax wrongly assessed and collected has to start within three years after payment, and an appeal that ends in a lower value triggers a refund automatically once the final value is set.

The same applies to 2026 temporary bills, which rested on 2025 millage rates and a partial digest. Hold on to the receipt for any estimate payment and compare it with the final bill before closing.

Georgia separately taxes recording of a long term real estate note, at $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of $500, and the security instrument must be recorded within 90 days. Ask the Clerk of Superior Court who collects it in Fulton County.

faqs.q: Does the county commissioner collect Alpharetta city tax?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner's list of cities it collects for leaves out Alpharetta, which keeps its own property tax accounts.

faqs.q: Why did my 2026 Fulton County bill look like an estimate?
faqs.a: The digest was late, so a court order allowed temporary bills based on 2025 millage rates. A refund or revised bill may follow.

faqs.q: Where can I visit a tax office in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: The Fulton customer service center is at 11575 Maxwell Road. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the number is 404-613-6100.

faqs.q: How long is the appeal window in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice mailing, filed with the county assessors.

faqs.q: Who covers transfer tax in Alpharetta?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under state law, though the contract can reassign it.
